title: Microsoft offers around 60,000 employees voluntary buyouts
detail:
Microsoft offers around 60,000 employees voluntary buyouts
The offer will be made available to employees on select teams across the US, Canada, India and the United Kingdom "at level 70 and below," meaning some senior staff could be included. Around 60,000 employees are reported to be eligible.
Nathan Rennolds
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 4:25 PM EDT 1 min read
MSFT
Trade MSFT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

US tech giant Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to employees around the globe, its chief people officer announced on Monday.

In a memo sent to staff, Amy Coleman called the "Voluntary Exit Offer" an "important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter."

The offer will be made available to employees on select teams across the US, Canada, India and the United Kingdom "at level 70 and below," meaning some senior staff could be included.

"This is a time-limited, voluntary program that gives those who are eligible the opportunity to leave Microsoft with financial support and career planning resources," the memo continued.

It added that eligible employees would receive an email with a link to their offers in the coming hours.

Around 60,000 staff are reported to be eligible.

In July, Microsoft announced it was eliminating around 4,800 roles, or roughly 2.1% of its global workforce at the time, as the company sought to shift its focus and cut costs as the AI era continues to take hold. Those cuts mostly affected the firm's commercial and Xbox gaming divisions.

Microsoft also offered some staff the option to retire early this year.

The company has said that more than 30% of those eligible for the early retirement scheme chose to participate and that it would "continue exploring similar approaches in the future."

title: Microsoft Offers Voluntary Separation to Employees Across Four Countries
detail:
PREMIUM
Microsoft Offers Voluntary Separation to Employees Across Four Countries
MT Newswires
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 4:00 PM EDT 2 min read
MSFT
Trade MSFT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
microsoft -Shutterstock

Microsoft (MSFT) will offer voluntary buyouts to employees in four countries including the US and India, with about 60,000 workers reportedly eligible for the program.

The voluntary separation program offers eligible workers a chance to leave the company with financial support and career planning resources, Microsoft Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said in a blog post. The program is available to employees in Canada and the UK too.

While Coleman did not specify the number of eligible employees, several news outlets, including Reuters and Bloomberg News, put that number at about 60,000. Microsoft employed approximately 223,000 people on a full-time basis as of June 30, 2026, according to its annual filing.

"The voluntary exit offer reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter," Coleman said. "This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the voluntary retirement program."

The technology sector has seen the biggest number of job cuts among industries in the US this year, totaling nearly 166,000 as of September, up 54% year over year, according to a recent report by Challenger Gray & Christmas.

The outplacement firm said that job cuts this year were driven by a number of factors, including artificial intelligence.

Coleman said in July that Microsoft was eliminating around 4,800 roles, or about 2.1% of the company's global workforce to align "our investment, people, and energy to our business priorities." The changes mostly targeted its commercial and Xbox divisions, she said at the time.

Earlier this year, the company offered voluntary buyouts to about 7% of its US workforce, reflecting about 9,000 roles, Reuters reported.

Microsoft is scheduled to release its fiscal first-quarter results on Wednesday.

Shares of the company were up 1.4% ahead of market close on Monday, taking the stock's year-to-date gain to about 10%.

title: Why Did Microsoft Stock Beat UiPath Over Five Years?

Why Did Microsoft Stock Beat UiPath Over Five Years?

Two software companies grew their sales at about the same pace over the last three years. Yet over the five years to October 2026, Microsoft (MSFT) stock gained 76.8%, while UiPath (PATH) lost 72.2%. So where did the gap come from: faster sales growth, bigger profits, or investors paying more for each dollar of sales?

Who Has Beaten UiPath Over Five Years?

Much of the industry had a difficult five years, with the median Systems Software stock falling 49.7% over the five years to October 2026. Even so, UiPath's stock did better than only 33.8% of the 68 companies in that industry.

Nine companies with sales growth similar to UiPath's had stocks that did better. The table shows two of them, Microsoft and Fortinet. Microsoft's stock finished 149.0 points ahead over five years.

Fortinet (FTNT), which sells cybersecurity products, finished even further ahead of UiPath, outperforming it by 240.6 points.

Did Microsoft Grow Faster Than UiPath?

Not by much. Over the last three years, UiPath expanded its sales by an average of 14.5% a year, tracking closely with the 16.1% pace at Microsoft. Between 2021 and 2026, UiPath actually recorded higher sales growth, climbing 133.5% compared with 97.4% for Microsoft.

Microsoft sells software, cloud services, and devices, ranging from Office and the Azure cloud platform to Xbox. Since Microsoft's sales grew only slightly faster over three years, and more slowly over five, faster growth does not explain why Microsoft's stock did so much better.

Where Did The Gap Come From?

Profit per share explains part of Microsoft's own gain. Microsoft increased its earnings per share by 123.1% between 2021 and 2026, a pace faster than its sales growth, while widening its operating margin by 5.2 points.

UiPath experienced a much larger margin movement. The company shifted from an operating loss equal to 51.9% of its sales in the twelve months to July 2021 to an operating profit of 8.9% of sales in the twelve months to July 2026.

The rest of the answer lies in what investors pay. Because UiPath had no profit in 2021, the two companies are compared on price-to-sales: at the end of June 2021, investors paid 48.5 times sales for UiPath and 12.1 times for Microsoft. At the Oct 23, 2026 close, they paid about 4.3 times for UiPath and about 11.7 times for Microsoft. The multiple accounts for most of the difference. UiPath improved its business more than Microsoft did, but investors now pay a small fraction of what they once paid for each dollar of UiPath's sales.

title: Brazil markets battered after Lula win, AI in focus elsewhere
detail:
Brazil markets battered after Lula win, AI in focus elsewhere
AFP
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 4:16 PM EDT 4 min read
Anthropic's stock market listing will test investor appetite to continue funding AI development (ANDREJ IVANOV)

Brazilian markets took a battering Monday following the shock reelection of leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, but elsewhere investors were focused on artificial intelligence (AI) technology companies.

Lula came from behind to win in the second-round vote, but his right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro, has vowed to challenge the result.

Brazilian markets reeled as trading got under way, but pared some of the steepest losses by the close. The Sao Paulo stock exchange plummeted by 13.7 percent to near a two-month low, with the real down around 8.5 percent against the dollar.

"Instead of fiscal consolidation under Bolsonaro, Brazilian assets are instead going to have to contend with Lula's campaign pledges, including a shorter working week," said Chris Turner at ING bank.

Elsewhere, investors geared up for the week's crucial run of central bank decisions and tech earnings for major companies.

"The AI complex remains under a microscope ahead of what may be the most important stretch of earnings season so far," noted SPI Asset Management's Stephen Innes.

"Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon are about to walk on stage, and this is not one of those quarters where a company can simply beat the number, raise the guidance by a whisker and expect applause. Investors want proof now.

"They want to know whether the billions going into the compute buildout are building a durable earnings machine or just a shinier version of the same old capex furnace," Innes added.

This week also sees the release of earnings from South Korean chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung.

- Testing investor appetite -

Results from Tesla and Meta last week stoked spending worries that weighed on stock markets.

Nevertheless, Meta announced Monday it was launching a stock offering that aims to raise $35 billion to fund its AI ambitions.

The parent company of Facebook and Instagram also announced plans to launch an additional stock offering of up to $60 billion, at a date yet to be determined.

Meta's shares fell by 1.88 percent at the close.

Anthropic, one of the world's leading artificial intelligence companies, on Monday made public its plans to sell shares on the stock market in mid-November.

The company reported first-half revenue up about 1,300 percent year-over-year, but also flagged safety risks.

Wall Street's main indices closed higher on Monday, with the tech-rich Nasdaq gaining 0.8 percent.

"Tech is once again mounting an attempt to rally, like a battered prize fighter getting up off the floor," said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at online trading and investing platform IG.

Anthropic's IPO Will "Suck a Massive Amount of Money" From AI Stocks, Cramer Warns ©TIKR
Key Takeaways

Meta Platforms launched $35 billion of stock offerings on Monday and plans a separate $60 billion program in 2027, on the same day Anthropic reportedly planned to file publicly for its IPO.

Jim Cramer warns that Anthropic's listing will pull money away from the rest of the AI group, a group that includes Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet.

Nvidia's forward P/E is at 17x, the low of its three-year range, even though analysts' estimate of its fiscal 2028 earnings has risen 25% since the end of June.

Microsoft looks the most exposed: it trades at 27x forward earnings, and its three-year low is 19x.

AI investors are about to be asked for a lot more money.

On Monday, Meta Platforms (META:NASDAQ) launched $35 billion of stock offerings. That same morning, Anthropic planned to make its IPO filing public, Bloomberg reported. The Claude maker reportedly expects its IPO to match or beat the size of SpaceX's.

Nvidia (NVDA:NASDAQ) wants a piece of Meta's deal too. It's one of three chipmakers that said they might buy up to $5 billion of Meta's new shares, though none of them has committed.

Jim Cramer saw this problem coming. On Mad Money a week ago, he warned that Anthropic's listing will "suck a massive amount of money away from the rest of the group" just because Anthropic is so big.

That group includes Microsoft (MSFT:NASDAQ), Amazon (AMZN:NASDAQ) and Alphabet (GOOG), and all three report earnings this week.

And Meta is just getting started.

Meta's share count is headed the other way

For years, Meta has been shrinking its diluted share count. It fell about 10% from fiscal 2021 to fiscal 2025, to 2.57 billion.

Meta Platforms (META): diluted shares outstanding, billions of shares, fiscal 2021–2025 (TIKR)

Now Meta is adding stock. The new deals are $22.5 billion of Class A shares and about $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred stock, with a separate $60 billion at-the-market program planned for 2027. Meta expects $135 billion to $145 billion of capex this year. It plans to pay for that with operating cash flow, investment-grade debt, partnerships and new stock.

Daniel Niles, a veteran tech investor, pointed out on X that Meta said in a recent filing that everyone is competing for the same pool of money. In his view, that pool "no longer seems endless like it did back earlier in the year."
